validity.researcher_notes: GEM's Capacity = 180 MMcf/d for this row traces, via the gem.wiki page's own citation [3], to the harvested Vaquero Midstream investor-conference PDF (lbcg.com, 'day-1-kirk-blackim...vaquero-midstream.pdf', Nov. 2018) -- confirmed live and downloaded (pdftotext -layout; url_verifier confirms 200, but its content-substring check misses on this large PDF, a documented false-negative pattern for big PDFs per url_verifier.py's own docstring, so I read it directly). That deck is a Permian Basin gathering/processing overview for Vaquero Midstream's Caymus plant. It never once names 'Atmos Pipeline-Texas' or 'Atmos Pipeline Texas' as a subject -- the sole 'Atmos' references are to a single 16-inch residue-gas interconnect labeled 'Atmos Line X-2' at the Caymus plant tailgate, with capacity given as '180,000 Mcfd' (=180 MMcf/d), alongside sibling interconnects (Northern Natural 30", Enterprise 36", ONEOK OWT 60,000 Mcfd, etc.). That is the capacity of ONE Permian-Basin delivery interconnect into the APT system, not APT's own system-wide transmission capacity -- the wiki editor appears to have misattributed a single-interconnect figure from a slide deck to the whole ~5,700-mile, 831-Bcf/yr statewide network. Independent scale check: Atmos Energy Corp's own May 2025 investor 'Analyst Update' deck (s201.q4cdn.com, live, confirmed via pdftotext) states APT 'Transported approximately 831 Bcf in Fiscal 2024 -- Average throughput of 2.3 Bcf/d' (=2,300 MMcf/d), i.e. average throughput alone is already >12x the recorded 180 MMcf/d 'capacity'. (Throughput is not identical to nameplate capacity, so I am not proposing 2,300 as a direct replacement value -- but it firmly establishes the current 180 MMcf/d figure is not credible for the whole system.) Both underlying documents are real and live; the defect is a citation/attribution mismatch, not a fabricated ref. Only 1 of the row's 3 harvested wiki citations bears on this issue (opened 3/3 -- see the existence note above for the other two).
